newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity prices rise with natural gas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity prices rise with natural gas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were higher Tuesday, boosted by stonger natural gas prices due to cold weather and lofty western physical prices, industry sources said.

As of 1230 EST, NYMEX February California Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures were up $1.10 at the day's high of $15.50 after morning exchanges as low as $14.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), while March COB was trading up 30 cents at $12.70.

February Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 87 cents at $17.40 per MWh after trades in a range of $17.25-17.60 per MWh, while March PV was bid at $14.45 and offered at $15.00 from Monday's settle at $14.50 per MWh.
Pressure was seen on electricity futures from higher natgas, where NYMEX February Henry Hub gas futures were up 10.6 cents at $3.36 per million British thermal units at 1245.

While western physical electricity prices were reported to be off Monday's highs, values remained pricey amidst cold weather through much of the U.S., with next day PV and COB set in the mid-40s per MWh, sources said.
While Bonneville Power Administration knocked $5 off of its peak power offers for Wednesday, prices remained comparatively high at $40.00 per MWh in the Northwest, the sources said.
Separately, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant in Page, Ariz., was back up to 720 MW after tripping off-line early Monday, sources familiar with the plant said.
Also, the 790 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant near Laughlin, Nevada, was back up to 650 MW where it will remain due to cooling tower restrictions, sources said.
Washington Public Power Supply System's 1,158 megawatt (MW) nuclear unit near Richland, Wash., was also expected to run at full rates at least through Friday, a spokesman for the plant said.
NYMEX said as of 1220 EST an estimated total of 94 COB and 106 PV contracts had traded.
COB open interest for Jan 13 fell 102 to 3,236 while PV open interest fell eight to 1,359, NYMEX said.
